items.evidence: After a page.reload() the test asserts the total equals money(expectedTotal) and the manual row shows 25% and the manual discount amount (spec lines 101-107). Those values only come back if the server saved the discount.

All three criteria are asserted. The total is checked against promoted less 25% (line 80). The manual row shows 25% with the reason, next to the promotion row (lines 89-96). The total and breakdown are checked again after a reload (lines 101-109).
It reuses DraftOrderPage.create, addProduct, total, discountToggle, summary, dialog and statusInfo. It adds no duplicate page object, GraphQL helper or scenario constant.
There is no waitForTimeout, sleep or polling loop. Waits are web-first assertions or dialog.waitFor({ state: 'hidden' }).
It imports test and expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and does not write to the cache or the dumps.
Locators use test ids, roles with names, or listitem filtered by hasText, all scoped to draft.summary or draft.dialog. There are no CSS classes, XPath or positional indexes.
The draft is started with DraftOrderPage.create and the product and promotion come from ORDERS_SCENARIO. Nothing is arranged through the API.
Expected amounts come from PRODUCTS.tee and PROMOTIONS. There are no hard-coded ids and no populatedb values.
It uses the fixture's default admin session. There is no UI sign-in and no credentials.
The spec lives at e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts, and typecheck.txt reports 'exit 0: no errors'.

e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts:34-37 (diff lines 40-43) and :74-76 (diff lines 80-82): the spec defines the Add Discount button, subtotal amount, manual and promotion row locators, and the multi-step fill-and-submit discount action inline instead of on DraftOrderPage.
The change adds no page-object members.
It has // Arrange (line 20) and // Act & Assert (line 44), the suite's own interleaved form.
It is one test for one story, with a test.step for each stage.
The title states the behaviour ('A 25% manual order discount applies on top of the tee's catalogue promotion and is saved') and carries #e2e.
The JSDoc header at lines 8-11 says what the spec covers and why: a manual discount on top of the catalogue promotion, persisted on the server.
Every assertion is web-first on a locator.

It derives amounts from the scenario constants, guards the threshold (line 32), formats money with toFixed(2) and imports ORDERS_SCENARIO. The 25% comes from the ticket, and the scenario has no constant for it.
There is no cleanup and there are no unique names.
There are no explicit timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call.

Add one E2E Tee', '// 6. Fill the value and reason, then confirm') restate the next line, and lines 1-2 point to spec and seed files that do not exist.

structured_output.summary: The test is sound: it proves the 25% manual discount is saved by reloading the page, covers all three acceptance criteria, reuses the DraftOrderPage flows, and passes the type check. It has two minor problems: locators and the discount-dialog action are written inline in the spec instead of on DraftOrderPage (M1), and its comments are generated numbered steps plus spec/seed header lines that point to files that do not exist (M13).
